newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury says 16 week sales up 4.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury says 16 week sales up 4.2 pct.

text.p: British supermarket J. Sainsbury Plc said on Wednesday that like-for-like sales rose 4.2 percent in the 16 weeks to the end of June.
In a statement to the annual meeting, Sainsbury said total sales were up 8.3 percent despite a decline in sales inflation because of lower fruit and vegetable prices.
"Our sales growth has continued to exceed industry averages. We expect to sustain like-for-like sales growth above inflation in the year ahead," chairman David Sainsbury said.
He warned, however, that sales inflation could fall further until late summer. Gross margins in food retailing were stable although competition remained intense, Sainsbury said.
Like-for-like do-it-yourself sales at the Homebase home improvement chain grew nine percent in the 16 weeks although sales of kitchens remained poor.
Sales at the the group's Savacentre hypermarkets and its U.S. unit Shaw's remained stable, Sainsbury said.
